item.title: Georgia developer's 30% profit-sharing claim rejected in October 29 appeals ruling
item.description: The business collaboration between Bruce Mortimer and Jeff White culminated in a legal clash centered on a software project. Jeff contended he was promised future profits and operational privileges. However, the Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that an enforceable partnership agreement was lacking due to vague terms. Consequently, White's claims regarding unpaid services and intellectual property were dismissed, highlighting the necessity of explicitly outlining business agreements.

item.title: Seven heirs of Jewish banker challenge Sotheby’s £1.2 million Pissarro sale, claim painting was looted by Nazis during World War II
item.description: A prized artwork by Camille Pissarro is embroiled in a contentious legal battle initiated by the heirs of Salomon Flavian. They assert that the piece was taken by the Nazis during WWII and argue that they were not adequately involved in a prior settlement. Sotheby’s counters, insisting the sale was aboveboard and legally sound. This dispute highlights ongoing hurdles in recovering Holocaust-era property and ensuring rightful family representation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hope Diamond Mailed To Museum: Harry Winston posts $1 million gem; plain parcel reshapes its legacy
item.description: The Hope Diamond embarked on a remarkable journey in 1958 when it was sent as registered mail to the Smithsonian Institution for safekeeping. This precious gem, with its origins in India, has a captivating royal history. American jeweller Harry Winston generously donated it to the museum after obtaining it from Evalyn Walsh McLean's estate in 1949.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 82% disapprove of Trump. So why are fewer Indian Americans identifying as Democrats?
item.description: Ahead of the November 3 US midterms, fresh polling shows Indian-Americans strongly favour Democrats on the economy and in congressional races. But a six-year decline in Democratic identification, growing political exhaustion and dissatisfaction with both parties suggest a more complicated relationship with the party.
item.dc:creator: Arghya Prasun Roychowdhury

item.title: In 1901,sponge divers off the Greek island of Antikythera recovered a gear from 2,000 years ago
item.description: In 1900, a remarkable discovery was made when divers stumbled upon the Antikythera Mechanism amidst a shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea. This ancient artifact showcased astounding knowledge of astronomy and mechanical engineering dating back over 2,000 years. Researchers found it capable of calculating astronomical cycles and predicting eclipses, intertwining science with the cultural tapestry of ancient Greece.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: In 2003, archaeologists in London found a tin pot nearly 2,000 years old full of face cream
item.description: In a remarkable find in 2003, archaeologists unveiled a cosmetic cream container dating back almost 2,000 years in London. Composed of animal fat, starch, and tin oxide, this ancient formula likely served as a moisturizer. Researchers painstakingly recreated the cream to explore its texture and look on the skin, shedding light on the beauty rituals of the past and our enduring human connection to history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Man Turns 600-Sq-Ft Apartment Plant Business Into Million-Dollar Venture in Six Years
item.description: Brandon Hurst began his journey into plant selling in 2020 as a side project to boost his income. What started as a small venture has blossomed into a thriving family enterprise, with annual sales surpassing 100,000 plants. Leveraging social media, he incorporated livestream auctions that dramatically boosted profits. Now operating from a vast 3,000-square-foot greenhouse in Los Angeles, Hurst aims to expand while ensuring meaningful connections with his customers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Buyers' promise to save Melbourne family home moves longtime owners to tears
item.description: In a heartfelt farewell, a Melbourne couple bid adieu to their beloved Maidstone home, a cherished sanctuary for over four decades after immigrating from Lebanon in 1982. Reassured by the buyers' intention to cherish the house rather than demolish it, the couple found solace in their memories. This sale marks a poignant shift as they prepare to embrace a new chapter in Taylors Lakes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2014, the 5.5-carat Ocean Dream sold for about $8.5 million; in May 2026 the same blue-green diamond, the largest of its kind known, sold at Christie’s Geneva for $17.3 million, roughly double
item.description: Ocean Dream, a unique blue-green diamond weighing 5.50 carats, was auctioned at Christie's Geneva for $17.3 million. This diamond, initially sold in 2014 for approximately $8.5 million, experienced a significant increase in value. Its distinct colouring results from natural radiation exposure during its geological formation. Notably, the Ocean Dream was previously showcased at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in 2003.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Persson Lists Beverly Hills Mansion: asks $70 million again; ultra-luxury LA market cools
item.description: Markus Persson, the mastermind behind Minecraft, is putting his lavish Beverly Hills mansion on the market for $70 million. This expansive property boasts eight bedrooms and 15 bathrooms, along with one-of-a-kind features like a candy room and a nightclub. Acquired in December 2014 after selling Mojang to Microsoft, this listing highlights both the opulence of the home and the difficulties of navigating the high-end Los Angeles real estate landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: UK PM rejects slavery reparations despite Caribbean demands, open to formal apology
item.description: The transatlantic slave trade lasted from the 15th to the 19th century, during which millions of Africans were captured, transported and sold into slavery by European traders. According to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database, Britain transported an estimated 3.2 million Africans across the Atlantic. At least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and forced into the trade.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Georgia woman wins $975,000 after falling at Walmart, but appeals court overturns verdict
item.description: A Georgia woman who won $975,000 after a fall at a Walmart store in 2020 will face a new trial after an appeals court overturned the verdict on October 29. The court found that her lawyer had improperly compared compensation for pain and suffering with an expert witness's $8,000 daily fee and minimum-wage rates. Judges ruled that these unrelated comparisons could have influenced the jury's decision.
